method: Simplified in-house Monte Carlo (not a validated code such as EGSnrc, Geant4 or PENELOPE). Point source with pyramid-uniform-in-solid-angle sampling, 1.6e7 histories, two lines equally weighted. Photon transport in homogeneous water with Klein-Nishina Compton (no binding), a power-law photoelectric term, an empirical Rayleigh term and a rough pair term. Track-length estimators in the 1 cm radius, 0.2 cm thick cylinder give fluences, process fractions and energy-transfer fractions; primary fluence checked against analytic exp(-mu*5 cm) (0.3% agreement). Electron initial spectra come from sampled Klein-Nishina and photoelectron kinematics. Electron fluence above 10 keV uses a continuous-slowing-down model with Moller delta-ray production and restricted stopping power, iterated to convergence. The energy-balance check FAILED by about 20%, so Layer 4 electron values are probably overestimated. Layer 3 spectra/direction, the Layer 4 angular distribution, the parent-scattered dose fraction, s_w,air and PDD5 are estimates, not computed results. D = K_col with beta = 1 (CPE), g from radiative/kerma energy ratio.
data_sources: Water electron density from standard composition (H 0.1119, O 0.8881 mass fractions, I = 75 eV). Klein-Nishina cross sections and energy-transfer cross sections computed analytically (checked against NIST water mu_en/rho ~0.47 at 1.25 MeV). Collision stopping power: Bethe formula, checked against ESTAR (22.56, 4.12, 2.03, 1.87 MeV cm2/g at 0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1 MeV). Radiative stopping: empirical ratio 0.0075*T to S_col. Moller delta-ray cross section from standard Moller formula, Rutherford limit normalization. Air I = 85.7 eV for stopping-power ratio. No NIST/ESTAR tables were loaded from files; values were reproduced from memory and analytic formulas.
